research_problem.title: Collatz Conjecture: New Computational Records for Delay/Glide Times and Verification Frontier
research_problem.summary: The Collatz conjecture (3n+1 problem) states that iterating f(n)=n/2 if even, f(n)=3n+1 if odd, always reaches 1. Despite being one of the most famous unsolved problems in mathematics, computational records for delay times (longest sequences before reaching 1), glide records (steps to first drop below starting value), and the verification frontier (largest N such that all integers up to N are confirmed to reach 1) remain improvable with clever algorithmic techniques. This project aims to either (a) find new delay/glide record holders beyond known records, (b) push the verification frontier using sieve-based and modular arithmetic acceleration, or (c) discover structural patterns in record-holders that yield novel mathematical insights. All results are trivially verifiable: given a claimed record number, a simple Python loop confirms the trajectory in seconds.
research_problem.why_its_hype: The Collatz conjecture is THE normie math problem. Erdos said 'mathematics may not be ready for such problems.' Any new record instantly trends. The verification is a 5-line Python script anyone can run.
research_problem.verification_method: def verify_collatz(n): steps=0; x=n; while x!=1: x=x//2 if x%2==0 else 3*x+1; steps+=1; return steps

items.description: Conduct comprehensive literature review on Collatz conjecture computational records
items.acceptance_criteria: Use websearch + semantic_scholar to find and document: (1) current delay record holders (known: ~8,528,817 steps for numbers near 2^68), (2) current verification frontier (known: verified up to ~2^68 by Barina 2021, Roosendaal ongoing), (3) best known algorithmic techniques (sieve methods, modular arithmetic shortcuts, Crandall's algorithm, tail optimization). At least 10 relevant papers cited in sources.bib. Create results/concept_evolve/tree/001_literature_review/literature_survey.json with structured findings.
items.notes: Comprehensive literature survey created. Key finding: Barina 2025 verified to 2^71, found 4 new path records. OEIS A284668 has 18 terms, a(19) is our target. 17 sources cited.

items.description: Build and maintain sources.bib with BibTeX entries for all consulted sources
items.acceptance_criteria: sources.bib in repo root contains valid BibTeX entries for at least 12 papers/sources including: Lagarias (1985) survey, Oliveira e Silva verification work, Barina (2020/2021) GPU verification, Roosendaal delay records database, Crandall (1978) algorithm, Tao (2019) almost all orbits result, Kontorovich & Miller stochastic models, Applegate & Lagarias density results. Each entry must have title, author, year, and URL/DOI fields.
items.notes: sources.bib created with 17 entries including all required sources. Each has title, author, year, and URL/DOI.

items.description: Survey existing code repositories and computational tools for Collatz computation
items.acceptance_criteria: Use websearch to find and document at least 5 existing open-source Collatz computation projects (e.g., Barina's GPU code, Roosendaal's tools, various GitHub repos). Create results/concept_evolve/tree/002_existing_tools/tool_survey.json listing each tool's language, approach, performance characteristics, and limitations. Identify the specific performance gap our approach will target.
items.notes: 6 tools surveyed. Performance gap identified: no existing tool targets OEIS A284668 specifically. Our approach: Python + gmpy2 + multiprocessing + k-step shortcut engine.

items.description: Concept-tree exploration: cross-domain techniques applicable to Collatz computation
items.acceptance_criteria: Use concept-tree-explorer subagent to explore connections between Collatz computation and: (1) number-theoretic sieves, (2) GPU parallel prefix algorithms, (3) probabilistic models of random walks, (4) automata theory / finite state transducers for Collatz iteration, (5) data compression / entropy coding for trajectory storage. Create results/concept_evolve/tree/003_cross_domain/ with concept.json and README.md documenting at least 6 cross-domain concept cards with implementation_hypothesis fields.
items.notes: 7 cross-domain concept cards created covering sieve adaptation, parallel prefix, random walk, FST, entropy-guided selection, trajectory compression, EVT prediction. ConceptEvolve kickoff already generated 12 concepts with 50 walk paths.

items.description: Implement naive Collatz iteration baseline in Python with timing benchmarks
items.acceptance_criteria: Create src/baseline.py implementing: (1) basic Collatz step function, (2) stopping time / delay time computation, (3) glide time computation (steps to first go below starting value), (4) trajectory recording. Benchmark on known record holders. Output: results/baselines/naive_benchmark.json with timing data for computing delay of numbers up to 10^9 (sampled), and verification of known delay records (e.g., 63,728,127 has delay 949).

items.description: Implement optimized Collatz iteration with standard tricks
items.acceptance_criteria: Create src/optimized.py implementing: (1) binary shortcut (process all trailing zeros at once via bit operations), (2) combined step (3n+1 is always even, so do (3n+1)/2 in one step), (3) lookup table for small values (precompute steps for n < 2^20), (4) tail-call optimization / iterative form. Benchmark shows at least 5x speedup over naive baseline on same test set. Output: results/baselines/optimized_benchmark.json.

items.description: Implement sieve-based verification for range checking
items.acceptance_criteria: Create src/sieve.py implementing Oliveira e Silva / Barina-style sieve: (1) for a range [a, b], use modular congruence classes to skip numbers guaranteed to converge quickly, (2) precompute which residue classes mod 2^k can be eliminated after k steps. Verify correctness by confirming all numbers up to 10^10 reach 1. Output: results/baselines/sieve_benchmark.json showing numbers checked per second and skip ratio achieved.

items.description: Define metrics framework and record verification protocol
items.acceptance_criteria: Create src/metrics.py and src/verify.py implementing: (1) delay time metric (total steps to reach 1), (2) glide time metric (steps to first drop below n), (3) max-excursion metric (highest value reached in trajectory), (4) compression ratio metric (ratio of starting value to trajectory length), (5) deterministic verification function that given (n, claimed_delay) returns True/False. Create results/metrics/metric_definitions.json. All metrics must match known values for benchmark numbers from Roosendaal's database.

items.description: Literature-graph-miner subagent: identify algorithmic acceleration techniques from adjacent fields
items.acceptance_criteria: Use literature-graph-miner subagent to mine citation graph starting from Barina (2021) GPU verification paper and Tao (2019) almost all orbits paper. Identify at least 3 underexplored algorithmic acceleration techniques from: (1) integer factorization sieve methods, (2) modular exponentiation chains, (3) parallel tree traversal algorithms. Create results/concept_evolve/tree/004_acceleration_techniques/ with concept.json documenting each technique's applicability to Collatz with estimated speedup factor.

items.description: Implement modular arithmetic shortcut engine (k-step lookahead tables)
items.acceptance_criteria: Create src/shortcut_engine.py implementing: For a given k (e.g., k=32 or k=40), precompute for each residue class r mod 2^k, the exact result of applying k Collatz steps symbolically: n -> (a*n + b) / 2^k where a,b depend on r. This allows processing k bits of n in a single arithmetic operation. Verify correctness on 10^6 random inputs. Benchmark shows at least 10x speedup over item_007 optimized baseline. Output: results/experiments/shortcut_engine_benchmark.json.

items.description: Implement delay record search algorithm targeting numbers beyond current known records
items.acceptance_criteria: Create src/delay_search.py implementing a targeted search for high-delay numbers using: (1) the known structure that record holders tend to have specific binary patterns, (2) priority queue of candidate numbers ranked by partial trajectory length, (3) early termination when trajectory drops below a known-verified threshold. Search space must cover numbers up to at least 2^70. Find and verify at least 3 numbers with delay > 1000. Output: results/experiments/delay_records.json with each record's n, delay, trajectory checkpoints, and verification status.

items.description: Concept-tree exploration: novel structural patterns in record-holding numbers
items.acceptance_criteria: Use concept-tree-explorer subagent to analyze binary representations of all known delay record holders (from Roosendaal's database, fetched via websearch). Identify structural patterns: (1) bit-density statistics, (2) autocorrelation of bit patterns, (3) relationship between binary structure and trajectory shape. Create results/concept_evolve/tree/005_structural_patterns/ with concept.json and pattern_analysis.json. Must propose at least 2 novel conjectures about the structure of delay-record numbers, each with a testable prediction.

items.description: Implement probabilistic model for predicting high-delay candidates
items.acceptance_criteria: Create src/probabilistic_model.py implementing Kontorovich-Miller style stochastic model: (1) model Collatz iteration as random walk with known bias, (2) compute expected delay given bit-length, (3) identify numbers whose actual delay significantly exceeds expected delay (these are interesting outliers). Use model to generate candidate lists for targeted search. Output: results/experiments/probabilistic_predictions.json with top-100 predicted high-delay candidates and their predicted vs actual delays.

items.description: Implement parallel/vectorized Collatz computation using numpy/multiprocessing
items.acceptance_criteria: Create src/parallel_collatz.py implementing: (1) batch trajectory computation using numpy integer arrays, (2) multiprocessing pool for embarrassingly parallel range checking, (3) efficient memory management for large trajectories. Benchmark on 8-core machine shows near-linear speedup (at least 6x on 8 cores). Can process at least 10^8 numbers per minute on commodity hardware. Output: results/experiments/parallel_benchmark.json.

items.description: Run comprehensive delay record search in range [2^60, 2^72]
items.acceptance_criteria: Execute delay_search.py with shortcut_engine and parallel computation targeting the range [2^60, 2^72]. Run for at least 2 hours of compute time. Produce results/experiments/full_search_results.json containing: (1) all numbers found with delay > 800 steps, (2) the top-10 highest delay numbers found with full verification, (3) comparison against Roosendaal's known record table. If a new delay record is found, document it with complete trajectory verification.

items.description: Verify all claimed records with independent verification script
items.acceptance_criteria: Create src/independent_verify.py as a completely separate, minimal implementation (under 50 lines, no optimizations, pure Python arbitrary precision) that verifies every claimed record from item_016. Output: results/experiments/verification_report.json with each record's (n, claimed_delay, verified_delay, match_status, verification_time_seconds). 100% of claimed records must verify correctly.

Each comparison must cite the specific source from sources.bib. Produce at least one figure (figures/throughput_comparison.png or .svg) showing performance comparison.

items.description: Statistical analysis of trajectory properties for discovered records
items.acceptance_criteria: Create src/trajectory_analysis.py analyzing all delay records found: (1) distribution of max-excursion / starting-value ratio, (2) distribution of steps-above-start / total-steps ratio, (3) correlation between bit-length and delay time with regression, (4) comparison of bit-density of records vs random numbers of same size. Output: results/experiments/trajectory_statistics.json and at least 2 figures in figures/ directory (delay_vs_bitlength.png, excursion_distribution.png).

Check if our observed patterns in record-holder binary structure have been previously noted. items.description: Create deterministic verification package for all results
items.acceptance_criteria: Create src/verify_all.py that: (1) reads all claimed records from results/experiments/, (2) independently verifies each one using the naive Collatz function, (3) outputs a single results/final/verification_certificate.json with every record, its verification status, and a SHA-256 hash of the verification computation. Running 'python src/verify_all.py' must complete in under 10 minutes and produce 100% pass rate. This is the 'anyone can check this' script.

items.description: Write comprehensive results summary with hype-worthy findings
items.acceptance_criteria: Create results/final/RESULTS.md documenting: (1) problem statement accessible to non-mathematicians, (2) our approach and key innovations, (3) headline results (new records found, with exact numbers), (4) performance metrics vs prior art, (5) novel structural conjectures with evidence, (6) complete references to sources.bib. Must be readable by someone with high school math. Include at least 3 embedded figures.

items.description: Generate Twitter/social media thread draft
items.acceptance_criteria: Create results/final/twitter_thread.md with a 5-10 tweet thread that: (1) opens with the headline result (new Collatz delay record or verification milestone), (2) explains the problem in one tweet, (3) shows the key number and its verification, (4) links to the verification script, (5) presents the most surprising finding. Each tweet must be under 280 characters. Must include a 'anyone can verify this in Python' code snippet.
